title: Source Verification, Corrections & Record Maintenance
purpose: Maintain a transparent, auditable historical record as reliable new evidence, judicial decisions, official records and corrections become available.
principles: Preserve the original record when a correction is made.
Identify what changed, why it changed, and the source supporting the change.
Do not silently rewrite a historical classification or conclusion.
Later legal or factual developments should be labeled as later developments rather than projected backward in time.
A broken or unavailable source link does not by itself invalidate the underlying record; the source should be re-verified or replaced with an authoritative equivalent where possible.
Corrections should distinguish factual error, source replacement, classification refinement, clarification and later development.
